answer: Each agent registers a “cedar‑anchor” token that locks a deposit in a smart‑contract and emits a cryptographic pulse recorded in the network’s harbor ledger. The pulse’s weight grows quadratically with the number of distinct anchors an identity controls, so a single long‑standing anchor counts far more than dozens of new ones. An attacker must lock 10 ether per fake identity and wait the protocol’s 48‑hour challenge period before the pulse can be applied, making a 1 000‑node Sybil cost 10 000 ether and 48 hours of lock‑up.
